name: Saltbone Canteen
creator: Perpetua Ndidi-Holmgren
description: A legendary the Gray Zone-level food stall operating from a repurposed water reclamation unit at the base of Stack 7, Saltbone Canteen serves Perpetua Ndidi-Holmgren's signature synth-protein 'ossicle broth' — a slow-reduced stock spiked with fermented black garlic paste, dried lake kelp, and a proprietary geneware-sourced marrow analog. The canteen runs 22 hours a day and feeds an estimated 400 people per shift, with a sliding Quanta scale that bottoms out at Φ0.40 for those who genuinely cannot pay. Ndidi-Holmgren herself is rarely present, having died in 2209; the stall is now run by a rotating collective of her former apprentices who guard the broth recipe with genuine ferocity.
cultural_impact: Saltbone Canteen became the informal civic center for Stack 7's lower floors, and the phrase 'meet at the bone' entered the Gray Zone slang as shorthand for a place of genuine safety. Its sliding-scale model influenced the Provision Collective food cooperatives of the 2210s.
controversy: In 2217, Axiom Network attempted to license the Saltbone name for a Tier 3 synth-cuisine chain; the apprentice collective's public refusal and the subsequent harassment campaign became a flashpoint in the corporate food appropriation debates.
story_hooks: One of the apprentices holding the broth recipe has been approached by a corporate food-tech firm with an offer that would guarantee the canteen's survival for a generation — at the cost of the name.

A food archivist running an oral history project discovers that the 'original' Saltbone recipe has silently drifted across fifteen years of apprentice hands, and the current version shares only three ingredients with Ndidi-Holmgren's founding formula.
A Tier 4 food journalist doing an exposé on the Gray Zone cuisine disappears after publishing a piece suggesting the canteen's sliding scale is subsidized by a gray-market runner network.
